source_text: Porro si dissensiones et schismata increpat, quae sine dubio mala sunt, et in continenti haereses subiungit. Quod malis adiungat, malum utique profitetur, et quidem maius, cum ideo credidisse se dicat de schismatibus et dissensionibus, quia sciret etiam haereses oportere esse. Ostendit enim gravioris mali conspectu de levioribus se facile credidisse, certe non ut ideo de malis crediderit quia haereses bonae essent, sed uti de peioris quoque notae temptationibus praemoneret non esse mirandum quas diceret tendere ad probabiles quosque manifestandos, scilicet quos non potuerint depravare. Denique si totum capitulum ad unitatem continendam et separationes coercendas sapit, haereses vero non minus ab unitate divellunt quam schismata et dissensiones, sine dubio et haereses in ea condicione reprehensionis constituit in qua et schismata et dissensiones: ac per hoc non eos probabiles facit qui in haereses diverterint, cum maxime diverti ab eiusmodi obiurget, edocens unum omnes loqui et id ipsum sapere, quod etiam haereses non sinunt.
thought_title: Heresies are reproved as a greater evil among divisions
orientation: Tertullian is commenting on Paul's words about divisions and heresies, arguing that Paul counted heresies among evils, not goods.
pass_a_gloss: Furthermore, if he rebukes dissensions and schisms, which without doubt are evils, he also immediately attaches heresies. What he attaches to evils, he certainly declares to be an evil, and indeed a greater one, since he says that he believed about schisms and dissensions for this reason, because he knew that heresies also had to exist. For he shows that at the sight of a more serious evil he easily believed about the lighter ones, certainly not that he believed about evils for this reason because heresies were good, but so that he might warn in advance about temptations of a worse kind also, that it was not to be wondered at, which he said tend toward making manifest each of the approved, namely those whom they could not corrupt. Finally, if the whole chapter aims at maintaining unity and restraining separations, but heresies tear away from unity no less than schisms and dissensions, without doubt he also places heresies in that condition of reproof in which he also places schisms and dissensions: and through this he does not make those approved who have turned aside into heresies, since he especially rebukes turning aside from such things, teaching all to speak one thing and to think the same thing, which heresies also do not allow.

choices.why: The term means those who have been tested and found genuine, matching the context of manifesting the faithful.

choices.english: places in that condition of reproof
choices.why: Preserves the legal flavor of 'condicio' as a status or category, and 'reprehensio' as blame or censure.
rejected: assigns to the same category of censure

choices.term: unum omnes loqui et id ipsum sapere
choices.english: all to speak one thing and to think the same thing
choices.why: Keeps the double infinitive structure and the literal sense of 'sapere' as to think or be minded.
rejected: all to say the same thing and hold the same opinion

choices.english: at the sight of a more serious evil
choices.why: Renders 'conspectus' literally as sight or view, preserving the visual metaphor.
rejected: in view of a greater evil

bible_refs.note: Tertullian refers to Paul's statement that heresies must exist so that the approved may be made manifest.

pass_b_english: Moreover, if Paul rebukes dissensions and schisms, which are without doubt evil, he immediately attaches heresies to them. By joining them to evils, he certainly declares heresies to be an evil, and a greater one at that, since he says he believed about schisms and dissensions because he knew that heresies also had to exist. For Paul shows that at the sight of a more serious evil he readily believed about the lesser ones. Certainly he did not believe about the evils because heresies were good, but rather to warn in advance that there should be no surprise at temptations of a worse kind as well, temptations which, he says, tend to make manifest those who are approved, namely those whom they could not corrupt.

Finally, if the whole passage aims at maintaining unity and restraining separations, and heresies tear people away from unity no less than schisms and dissensions do, then without doubt Paul places heresies in that condition of reproof in which he also places schisms and dissensions. And for this reason he does not make those approved who have turned aside into heresies, since he especially rebukes turning away from such things, teaching all to speak one thing and to think the same thing, which heresies do not allow.

polish.changed: Clarified that Paul is the subject throughout, replaced ambiguous pronouns with explicit names, and broke the long passage into two paragraphs at the natural turn in the argument.

notes.quote: For he shows that at the sight of a more serious evil he readily believed about the lesser ones.
notes.why: 'He' is Paul but the referent is unclear; reader may think it refers to Christ from the previous section.
